chapter_title: The Catechumen asks the Apostle: will Rest come ab

fills.notes: The line needs a temporal anchor: entreaty exists from the primordial beginning; in the oldest layer this is stated as a continuous practice starting at the first emergence of the Light powers. The next clause begins with “the gods first made entreaty…”, so a simple temporal phrase best matches the impersonal cosmological register.

fills.fill: and they shall receive from them
fills.notes: The sentence contrasts (a) how they beseech from the first ones with (b) in what form they entreat their request; then it should conclude with the outcome: receiving “every thing”.
Needs an adverbial clause: he gives ease in the land of rest “as is fitting for the Living Spirit…”. This keeps the substrate’s impersonal, correspondential tone.

fills.fill: the first giver of ease, according to
fills.notes: The sequence repeats the title and then moves into “the will of these three”; a bridge phrase like “according to” (i.e., in accordance with) links his act to the triadic will (Father–Mother–First Man / or the three hypostases active here).

The surviving fragment “The welcomer [...] find with the welcomer that [...” is too broken; minimal connective restoration is all that is defensible without the underlying Coptic. The function is to resume narration after a titulary aside.

¶14 resumes the consequence of the Mother’s entreaty and introduces “a great power … the First Man…”. In the cosmogonic logic, the Mother (by granted entreaty) sends/commissions the Living Spirit to redeem the First Man.
The clause “a great power [...] of the loved one [...]” expects identification of the power: the Living Spirit is the “great power” given in ¶11 and is the agent of redemption here.

“of the loved one” in this register is commonly completed as a kinship term indicating derivation from the Father’s love; “son” fits the surrounding son-language already present in ¶10 (“son of God”).

Before “and they built the universe…”, a collective act of arranging/assembling is required. “elements” matches the later mention of “elements” (¶27) and the builder-theme of the oldest cosmological layer.
They request “the power … the leader, a guide…” which, in this system, is the Third Ambassador. A genitival pointer (“of the Third one”) anticipates the explicit naming in ¶19.
After “he received from them their prayer” the next move is divine assent leading to granting. “he was pleased” is a standard impersonal assent formula consistent with substrate tone.
“he summoned from him […] which is the Third Ambassador” needs “the power” as what is summoned forth from the Father’s treasury/majesty; fits the cosmological mechanics of emanation.

“the Ambassador […] in his charity” requires a verb of merciful inclination; “had compassion” preserves the structural (not moralistic) sense: the Light power turns toward what is bound to effect release.
“together with the […] of the Father” most naturally takes “entreaty”/“request” as the paired terms throughout the chapter; the triad’s will is fulfilled together with the Father’s granting act.
“the one that […] he gave the entreaty…” requires a prior reception/acceptance of prayer as the condition for giving. This also mirrors ¶19’s sequence (receive → give).

¶25 introduces “the third entreaty… third time” and then immediately narrates image-display/hiding—this is the Third Ambassador’s epiphany tactic to stir separation. So he must be the subject entering the scene.
“displayed his image” is typically done before the Archons/rulers of the Darkness as a lure/trigger for emission and separation; “rulers” keeps oldest-layer cosmology.

He “hid his image from the …” and then “stood firm … they revealed … the light …”. Hiding from the abyssal depth (the devouring field) fits the correspondential mechanics: concealment from those who would swallow, manifestation to those who will emit.
“he stood firm […] they revealed […] the light” implies stability of form/measure while others react. “form” matches the image/figure vocabulary.
A resumptive marker is expected in this highly compressed line to move from concealment to renewed revelation.
“they revealed … the light …” needs a dative; the revelation is ‘to them’ (to the opposing powers) as part of the separation process.
The sudden “the First Man … mock …” suggests a response by the Darkness powers when the archetypal combatant is evoked; “remembered” fits: they recall the First Man and begin derision.
Restores the verb explicitly demanded by “mock … to him…”.
Mockery issues from the opposite correspondence of height/pride; this also prepares for “which is exalted … garment …”.
“which is exalted” needs a noun: height/loftiness; correspondentially the false ‘height’ of Darkness opposes true height of Light.
“garment” here is the luminous investiture/appearance used in the epiphany. “robe of light” is the oldest-layer way to speak of the light-body/form.
“they were freed …” suggests a partial liberation at this stage (some light-elements released by the reaction).
Freedom in this mythic mechanism is coupled with return/ascent toward the Light treasury.
“their voice … the body … prayer …” points to a cry/voice rising from embodied soul as prayer-impulse awakened by the epiphany.
Voice/prayer arises from within the bound body (interior → exterior correspondence).
The whole section is about freeing; “bonds” matches “entangled and set fast” motifs repeated in ¶19, ¶31, ¶37.
¶26 continues the third entreaty sequence and needs a subject/action introducing a standing with the living ones. “came and stood” fits the theophanic/ordering pattern.
Matches the chapter’s repeated formula of standing to prayer (cf. ¶18).
“with the living ones and […] for ever” strongly suggests a promise of enduring life among the Living.
“the first […] from the […] he gave him the hope” expects “the first entreaty” / “first request” language reused structurally.
Standard source of granting/hope in this cosmological register; matches earlier “presence of the Father of Greatness.”
Hope given in this system is hope of ascent/return of the soul/light. Fits the immediate soteriological-cosmological motion without pastoral overlay.
“Jesus the Splendour perfected the will …” likely refers back to the five powers who prayed in ¶18. He perfects/fulfills their will by acting as revelatory power.
The paragraph later explicitly says “He granted the will of the elements.” Earlier “the will …” should match the same subject.
“they found the light …” in this myth is the elements/light-particles recognizing their kind through the appearing Splendour; restoring “elements” keeps coherence.
“the will of the …” most naturally “powers” (Light powers) in this register.
“that he had … he gave them the power” needs a prior commitment/ordinance—“promised” or “ordained”. “promised” is least intrusive.
Before “for ever” a stable-state verb is expected: stand/remain. Echoes “stood to prayer” but now as eternal standing in Light.
“This first […] he was humbled…” likely refers to “this first entreaty/first figure” within the third entreaty complex; “entreaty” best matches chapter vocabulary.
“he was humbled, he was made free …” needs an instrumental: by it (by this power/appearance) the bound one is humbled/freed.
“the [...]-ness is displayed to his enemies” points to the quality of splendour/brightness; completing as “Splendour-ness” keeps the proper name’s semantic force.
“He received the hope […] reveal […]” suggests “hope of release” awakened by revelation.
Jesus the Splendour reveals to those bound in mixture; this is the substrate’s functional definition of the revealer.
Ends with “and the entreaty of the […] of light …” The lacuna should supply the genitive: the first entreaty (i.e., the primordial plea) of the powers of light, keeping the entreaty-theme continuous.
“Now, just as this entreaty […]” requires the same fulfillment formula used earlier (receive/fulfill).
Sets up a correspondence: as the entreaty is, so is the figure/form that results.
The paragraph is about “figure” repeatedly: figure/l likeness/image as correspondential manifestation.
“that they have …” most naturally “established/constructed” in a cosmological teaching tone.
The section turns to epistemology (“Happen you know this: Every one … knows, he has perceived …”). “made known” fits.
Oldest layer: “figure” corresponds to an interior truth made visible in ultimates; “truth” is the spiritual degree underlying forms.
“you are set firm …” is firmness in understanding/knowledge rather than faith-exhortation; keeps impersonal didactic tone.
Strengthens the epistemic claim without turning pastoral.

The close “out from … within him … upon him …” demands the correspondential axiom: perception joins outer and inner; restoring as a balanced pair fits the doctrine of correspondences (inside→outside, yet read also outside→inside as sign).

¶31 begins an enumerated list (“The first: …”) and then defines a function “of the living soul … freed… by cause of him.” The agent is the revealer (Jesus Splendour / Third Ambassador in this complex). Oldest-layer functional title: “the revealer.”
“entangled […] entirely” most naturally completes with “in the universe”, a repeated scope-term in this chapter.
“He has […] his father” likely “seen”/“beheld” (vision of the Father) as a result of redemption; fits the ascent logic.
Pairs with earlier repeated epithet “the first established one” for the Father.
“the light has pity … the way also …” needs the subject explicitly: the Light (as power/realm) pities and opens a way.
“the way also …” is best completed as “opened (a way)” in redemption mechanics.
“a request […] affliction” suggests petitioning ‘for him from affliction’ (deliverance).
“Again, just as he has […] of the light” needs a verb parallel to “besought/claimed”: requested/asked of the Light powers.
Completes “of the light […]” as “powers” consistent with vocabulary.
“give ease for his […]” in this mythic register is often ‘brother’ (one soul aiding another of the same stock). This also anticipates ¶43’s co-helper motif.
Moves from present exemplar to future general rule (they shall grant…).
Ends with “come forth […] for ever.” The destination is the Light realm; this keeps the cosmological (not ecclesial) endpoint.

After “It goes into the land of light […] soul that was redeemed because of it …” the gap likely specifies that it enters with its own portion/measure of light reclaimed; this matches correspondential ‘measure’ language (portion of essence).
The cadence “land of life and rest …” closes naturally with the eternal-state marker already used elsewhere in the chapter.

assessment: Only a small subset of lacunae can be tightly restored from the provided English core because most gaps in ¶25–¶28 and ¶37 depend on lost Coptic syntactic cues and fixed Manichaean formulae. Where the correspondential cosmology strongly constrains the agent (Mother of Life → Living Spirit; Five → Third Ambassador; revealer → Jesus Splendour) restorations are moderate/strong. Many minor connectives are necessarily tentative/minimal. If you provide the Coptic line-breaks or any surviving letters for the brackets, the reconstructions can be made much tighter and expanded to all 92 lacunae.
